instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: Twenty and unknown in England; transformed Arsenal’s midfield within weeks of arriving.
Captain of an unbeaten title side. Physically dominant and technically excellent — genuinely world class.
Signed from Cambridge and broke his leg in his third start; a capable but still unproven top-flight forward at this point.
Regular first-team football at Coventry finally showed what he was, three years after the broken leg at United.
Eighteen goals, a share of the Golden Boot and an England cap: his peak.

Frozen out by Gullit and refused a squad number; the drop is partly the situation and partly a genuine decline at 32.
Nineteen, six starts, five goals — already an obvious top-flight footballer, not yet a starter.
A rung below the Keane anchor (91) in the same side and season; complete midfielder, not quite the driving force.
Back from Sampdoria and still one of England's quickest recovery defenders, though past the Italia 90 peak that sits outside this file.

Nine goals in eight starts on arriving from Trabzonspor. A hot streak in a relegation fight, not a step change in ability, so the rating moves three points and not nine.
The breakout: two goals in the League Cup final and Liverpool's most dangerous player.
Fifteen assists as a genuinely elite creator; the level that took him to Real Madrid as a starter.
England-capped and an ever-present, but technically limited enough that the caps are not evidence of ability here.
Ever-present in the title side and the best defender in it; quick, reads the game, unfussy.
A rotation option at United rather than a first choice, and injured for much of the treble season.
His best season, and a British record fee for a defender followed. The fee is not the reason for the number.
Ever-present and his best season; a shade above the 84 anchor rather than a different player.
Back trouble and a Middlesbrough side that asked far more of him at 33.
Seventeen, eleven starts; obvious ability, obviously raw.
Twenty and already England’s most complete young defender; a long way short of the 2007/08 anchor (91) but clearly elite-bound.
The season of his public confession and rehabilitation; he was some way short of himself on the pitch.
Restored, and arguably the best season of his career: ever-present, Arsenal's creative hub, and back in the England squad for Euro 96.

Ever-present in Bradford's survival season, which is evidence about a hard-working side rather than a step up in ability.
Took the Wimbledon shirt for good and became Scotland's first choice; a very good shot-stopper for a modest side.
PFA Team of the Year at 21; quick, aggressive and increasingly a genuine attacking threat.
Rated as the twenty-year-old breaking through in the double season, not the player of 1999.
Runner-up for the Ballon d’Or; the best right-sided midfielder in the world that season. Elite delivery and range of passing, ordinary one-v-one.
PFA and FWA Player of the Year in a double season. First touch and vision of an all-time great forward; held below 95 by the absence of pace and the modest goal volume.
Thirty-four and rotated through the Invincibles season; still the best technician in the side.
Rated as the 20-year-old breaking through after two broken legs, not the England player he became.
The rise from the 1992/93 rating spans two seasons lost to broken legs; he came back a materially better player and was an ever-present for a side that finished third.
Five starts before a knee injury he never properly recovered from; the pace never came back.
Thirteen years on and playing central midfield at 35; still a competent top-half regular.
Title winner and an England call-up; his peak.
Cruciate injury, ten starts.
